title: Undo a mistake
prompt: Someone ran a delete on every trail inside a transaction. Undo it, then delete only the North trails, which is what was wanted. Replace the ___.

check.sql: SELECT id, name FROM trails ORDER BY id;

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM trails; INSERT INTO trails VALUES (7, 'Birch Walk', 'West', 3.1, 40), (8, 'High Moor', 'East', 12.6, 610), (9, 'Crag Top', 'North', 6.0, 900);

solutions: BEGIN; DELETE FROM trails; ROLLBACK; DELETE FROM trails WHERE region = 'North';

title: Commit a change
prompt: Inside a transaction, delete the trails in the East region, and commit.

check.sql: SELECT id, name FROM trails ORDER BY id;

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM trails; INSERT INTO trails VALUES (7, 'Birch Walk', 'West', 3.1, 40), (8, 'High Moor', 'East', 12.6, 610), (9, 'Crag Top', 'North', 6.0, 900);

solutions: BEGIN; DELETE FROM trails WHERE region = 'East'; COMMIT;

wrongSolutions.sql: BEGIN; DELETE FROM trails WHERE region = 'East'; ROLLBACK;

title: Two changes together
prompt: In one transaction, raise book 1's price by 1 and lower book 2's by 1, then commit.
hints: Both UPDATEs go between BEGIN and COMMIT.

check.sql: SELECT id, title, author, genre, price, pages, year FROM books ORDER BY id;

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM books; INSERT INTO books VALUES (10, 'Copper Moon', 'Ada Hill', 'Fantasy', 20.0, 100, 2020), (11, 'North Light', 'Raj Dev', 'Travel', 7.5, 180, 2015), (12, 'Sky Atlas', 'Ada Hill', 'Science', 25.0, 300, 2023); INSERT INTO books VALUES (1, 'The Salt Road', 'Mina Rao', 'History', 18.5, 320, 2019), (2, 'Quiet Engines', 'Tom Okafor', 'Science', 24.0, 412, 2021);

solutions: BEGIN; UPDATE books SET price = price + 1 WHERE id = 1; UPDATE books SET price = price - 1 WHERE id = 2; COMMIT;

wrongSolutions.sql: BEGIN; UPDATE books SET price = price + 1 WHERE id = 1; COMMIT;
BEGIN; UPDATE books SET price = price + 1 WHERE id = 1; UPDATE books SET price = price - 1 WHERE id = 2; ROLLBACK;

title: Move a person
prompt: In one transaction, move employee 4 to department 3 and set their bonus to 500, then commit.
hints: Two changes, or a single UPDATE, inside the transaction.

check.sql: SELECT id, name, department_id, salary, bonus FROM employees ORDER BY id;

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM employees; DELETE FROM departments; INSERT INTO departments VALUES (5, 'Design'), (6, 'Finance'), (7, 'Ops'); INSERT INTO employees VALUES (11, 'Ivy', 5, NULL, 90000, '2019-02-01', 900, 'ivy@acme.test'), (12, 'Jon', 5, 11, 70000, '2020-06-15', NULL, NULL), (13, 'Kim', 6, 11, 70000, '2023-03-03', 300, 'kim@acme.test'), (14, 'Leo', NULL, 77, 30000, '2024-08-20', NULL, 'leo@acme.test'), (15, 'Mia', 6, 13, 55000, '2022-12-31', 0, 'mia@acme.test'); INSERT INTO employees VALUES (4, 'Dev', 2, 1, 70000, '2020-11-09', 2000, 'dev@acme.test');

solutions: BEGIN; UPDATE employees SET department_id = 3 WHERE id = 4; UPDATE employees SET bonus = 500 WHERE id = 4; COMMIT;
BEGIN; UPDATE employees SET department_id = 3, bonus = 500 WHERE id = 4; COMMIT;

wrongSolutions.sql: BEGIN; UPDATE employees SET department_id = 3 WHERE id = 4; COMMIT;
BEGIN; UPDATE employees SET department_id = 3, bonus = 500 WHERE id = 4; ROLLBACK;

title: Partial undo isn't automatic
prompt: Without using a transaction, an error doesn't undo earlier statements. Here, insert id 70, Ivy Path, North, 1.0, 10, on its own, with no BEGIN.
hints: A single statement saves on its own.

check.sql: SELECT id, name, elevation_m FROM trails ORDER BY id;

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM trails; INSERT INTO trails VALUES (7, 'Birch Walk', 'West', 3.1, 40), (8, 'High Moor', 'East', 12.6, 610), (9, 'Crag Top', 'North', 6.0, 900);

solutions: INSERT INTO trails (id, name, region, length_km, elevation_m) VALUES (70, 'Ivy Path', 'North', 1.0, 10);

wrongSolutions.sql: BEGIN; INSERT INTO trails (id, name, region, length_km, elevation_m) VALUES (70, 'Ivy Path', 'North', 1.0, 10); ROLLBACK;
INSERT INTO trails (id, name, region, length_km, elevation_m) VALUES (70, 'Ivy Path', 'North', 1.0, 11);

title: Fix the unfinished transaction
prompt: This should cancel order 2 and save the change, but it ends with the wrong command. Fix it.
hints: End with COMMIT to keep it.

check.sql: SELECT id, customer_id, status FROM orders ORDER BY id;

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM order_items; DELETE FROM orders; DELETE FROM products; DELETE FROM customers; INSERT INTO customers VALUES (7, 'Ravi', 'Oslo', 'ravi@mail.test', '2024-05-05'), (8, 'Sara', 'Lima', NULL, '2024-06-06'), (9, 'Tom', 'Oslo', NULL, '2024-07-07'); INSERT INTO products VALUES (7, 'Stool', 'Home', 40.0, 25.0), (8, 'Cup', 'Kitchen', 9.0, 2.0), (9, 'Ink', 'Stationery', 12.5, 6.0); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (11, 7, '2024-02-28', 'shipped'), (12, 8, '2024-03-01', 'pending'), (13, 7, '2024-03-31', 'cancelled'); INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (11, 7, 1, 4.0), (11, 8, 3, NULL), (12, 9, 2, NULL), (13, 8, 1, NULL); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (2, 9, '2024-04-01', 'pending');

solutions: BEGIN; UPDATE orders SET status = 'cancelled' WHERE id = 2; COMMIT;

wrongSolutions.sql: BEGIN; UPDATE orders SET status = 'cancelled' WHERE id = 2; ROLLBACK;
BEGIN; UPDATE orders SET status = 'cancelled'; COMMIT;

title: Archive and remove
prompt: In one transaction: add a product copy of product 1 with id 300, name Archived, the same category, price, and cost; then delete product 1. Commit.

check.sql: SELECT id, name, category, price FROM products ORDER BY id;

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM order_items; DELETE FROM orders; DELETE FROM products; DELETE FROM customers; INSERT INTO customers VALUES (7, 'Ravi', 'Oslo', 'ravi@mail.test', '2024-05-05'), (8, 'Sara', 'Lima', NULL, '2024-06-06'), (9, 'Tom', 'Oslo', NULL, '2024-07-07'); INSERT INTO products VALUES (7, 'Stool', 'Home', 40.0, 25.0), (8, 'Cup', 'Kitchen', 9.0, 2.0), (9, 'Ink', 'Stationery', 12.5, 6.0); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (11, 7, '2024-02-28', 'shipped'), (12, 8, '2024-03-01', 'pending'), (13, 7, '2024-03-31', 'cancelled'); INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (11, 7, 1, 4.0), (11, 8, 3, NULL), (12, 9, 2, NULL), (13, 8, 1, NULL); INSERT INTO products VALUES (1, 'Notebook', 'Stationery', 4.0, 1.5);

solutions: BEGIN; INSERT INTO products (id, name, category, price, cost) SELECT 300, 'Archived', category, price, cost FROM products WHERE id = 1; DELETE FROM products WHERE id = 1; COMMIT;

wrongSolutions.sql: BEGIN; DELETE FROM products WHERE id = 1; INSERT INTO products (id, name, category, price, cost) SELECT 300, 'Archived', category, price, cost FROM products WHERE id = 1; COMMIT;
wrongSolutions.why: The row is gone before copying

wrongSolutions.sql: BEGIN; INSERT INTO products (id, name, category, price, cost) SELECT 300, 'Archived', category, price, cost FROM products WHERE id = 1; COMMIT;

title: Salary swap
prompt: In one transaction, swap the salaries of employees 2 and 4, using the values 70000 and 95000 directly, then commit. Employee 2 gets 70000.

check.sql: SELECT id, name, department_id, salary, bonus FROM employees ORDER BY id;

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM employees; DELETE FROM departments; INSERT INTO departments VALUES (5, 'Design'), (6, 'Finance'), (7, 'Ops'); INSERT INTO employees VALUES (11, 'Ivy', 5, NULL, 90000, '2019-02-01', 900, 'ivy@acme.test'), (12, 'Jon', 5, 11, 70000, '2020-06-15', NULL, NULL), (13, 'Kim', 6, 11, 70000, '2023-03-03', 300, 'kim@acme.test'), (14, 'Leo', NULL, 77, 30000, '2024-08-20', NULL, 'leo@acme.test'), (15, 'Mia', 6, 13, 55000, '2022-12-31', 0, 'mia@acme.test'); INSERT INTO employees VALUES (2, 'Ben', 1, 1, 80000, '2019-07-01', NULL, NULL), (4, 'Dev', 2, 1, 60000, '2020-11-09', 2000, NULL);

solutions: BEGIN; UPDATE employees SET salary = 70000 WHERE id = 2; UPDATE employees SET salary = 95000 WHERE id = 4; COMMIT;

wrongSolutions.sql: BEGIN; UPDATE employees SET salary = 70000 WHERE id = 2; COMMIT;
BEGIN; UPDATE employees SET salary = 95000 WHERE id = 2; UPDATE employees SET salary = 70000 WHERE id = 4; COMMIT;
